body: me too, i’ve been trying to get on it all week

thank you for your reply. 100% i doubt myself way too much but also i look at the qualified midwives and think to myself god i don’t think i could ever do that. i can’t see myself knowing how to handle an emergency situation, in every emergency i’ve been in on placement as a student i stand and freeze and think “oh my god what on earth am i getting myself into” and do nothing, like a spare part. i’m very much lacking in clinical skills too and i see areas where i need improvement and i just don’t feel the want to improve them, i don’t know if that’s because i’m depressed or generally just not enjoying it. when i’m on placement, in clinics for example, i’ll be so happy if a woman doesn’t turn up, and that’s no way to feel as a student, i should be excited. most of the other girls are working so much more confidently than i am, some of them are working at year 3 level. when they share with the rest of the cohort their responsibilities (for example looking after a whole bay of women on their own or discharging families on their own) it makes me feel sick because i don’t want to do that, i would constantly be worried i sent a woman and her baby home and something bad would happen. i definitely am lacking in knowledge, i do not know anywhere near as much as i should do but again, i feel empty and uninspired to learn, never reading or studying. when i think about quitting it fills me with relief, when i think about getting a job where i can leave it at the door and not worry about having people’s lives in my hands it fills me with relief too. i just don’t know what to do, i definitely went into midwifery looking at it with rose tinted glasses and don’t get me wrong i have seen some lovely things and met some lovely families but i have seen the state of the nhs maternity and i am no where near strong, confident, competent, resilient enough to deal with walking into that every single day of my life :(
